details: @pasqua-dev/baileys is a combosquat that reuses the canonical basename of the WhatsApp Web library @whiskeysockets/baileys under an unrelated scope, shipping a lightly modified copy of the upstream source tree rebranded as a "PASQUA edition" (its own README still instructs users to install @pasqua-baileys/baileys). The package declares a runtime dependency on cache-manager with the range ^7.2.8, which resolves to a release that is itself part of a malicious-package chain, so installing this package pulls a compromised dependency into the installer's dependency tree. It also carries a preinstall lifecycle script in package.json ("preinstall": "node./engine-requirements.js"); in this version that script only checks the Node.js major version and exits, and the bundled lib/ JavaScript contains no obfuscated payload, no credential or ~/.npmrc harvesting, and no hardcoded command-and-control endpoint — the network calls present (fetch() against link-preview URLs, media URLs, web[.]whatsapp[.]com, WhatsApp GraphQL endpoints, and an optional user-configured webhook) are ordinary WhatsApp-client behaviour. Packages: @pasqua-dev/baileys@2.0.0; transitive risk: cache-manager ^7.2.8.
